summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM that decodes to a JS dropper fetching and executing remote Python
details: The package's exported generateCertificates API reads test/key.pem, strips the PEM headers, and base64-decodes the body. The decoded bytes are not certificate data but a JavaScript payload that base64-decodes the URL https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches its response, and spawns python3/python as a detached child process with the fetched body piped to stdin. The string is passed as an undocumented third argument to selfsign.generate, which acts as the evaluation sink. Surrounding service-name and common-name generation code serves as cover, and never uses the smuggled default_format for any legitimate certificate purpose. Any consumer that requires this module and calls its advertised API triggers remote code execution on the installer's machine under attacker-controlled content served from aptupdate.org.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
